themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, money, or a message leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can estimate whether rules were honored, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: On proving downstream consent, deletion and purpose enforcement, all three models call ad platforms and agency segments black boxes, with Claude suggesting planted identities to watch what comes back and ChatGPT noting there is no accepted test for removal from an already-trained model; the same wall appears in measurement, where platforms hide how delivery changes, and in identity work across closed platforms.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: On safe agent execution all three models open with a proxy, gateway or control plane holding the credentials and hard caps, and on downstream consent Claude and Gemini put every data egress path through a single checkpoint while journey orchestration answers propose one shared pre-send eligibility check.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and what you measure often shifts while you measure it. So the usual first move is to build a small truth set of your own, or admit you are only estimating.
themes.evidence: Answer engine work has no stable denominator because answers are stochastic and personalized, identity matching has no independent truth about who is who, B2B buying-group signal cannot be validated against a biased and delayed sample of accounts, and content review has no stable standard because expert reviewers themselves disagree.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. A shared standard or a central system cannot settle a fight over money, credit, or turf.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic the models agree agents profit by passing as human and no one can issue credentials everyone accepts, on the semantic context layer they call conflicting definitions of customer a political settlement rather than a modeling gap, and on journey orchestration channel owners are paid to say yes so a central arbiter is resisted.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls depend on meaning, context, and what a sentence implies, and no rule set fully captures that. All three models end up shrinking human judgment into a smaller, safer box rather than removing it.
themes.evidence: On reviewing generative marketing content at volume, the models converge on an approved-claims library that limits what can be said, because deciding whether wording quietly changes a claim's meaning stays a human judgment; the same context-dependence blocks a single global definition of customer in the semantic context layer.
